overall_summary: The channel's clear growth driver is extreme space and exoplanet anomalies, particularly when framed as high-stakes 'What If' hypothetical scenarios or showcasing bizarre planetary weather (e.g., burning ice, supersonic rubies, and coal-dark planets). Conversely, general psychology facts and basic animal trivia underperform significantly, failing to capture viewer curiosity in the highly competitive Shorts feed.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,025 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) are the channel's top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on bizarre planetary conditions, focusing on extreme temperatures, rains of strange materials (glass, rubies, iron), and mind-bending physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieved 951 views and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' secured 492 views with strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanet facts as first-person hypothetical survival scenarios to immediately hook the viewer's imagination and boost retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (multiple uploads ranging from 5 to 53 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out standard psychology facts unless they can be re-framed with a highly dramatic, cinematic, or survival-oriented hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 views) underperform compared to the cosmic content.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid dry, textbook-style animal facts. If covering biology, shift to cinematic animal survival stories with high narrative stakes.

next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the night side of this planet is cold enough to turn the iron vapor back into liquid, creating a literal, deadly metallic monsoon.
next_video.posting_window: Late afternoon (13:00 - 15:00 UTC) to capture peak active browsing times based on recent upload success.
next_video.reason: Combines the proven 'What If' hypothetical format with the highly engaging theme of extreme exoplanet weather (WASP-76b), leveraging the exact 21-second duration of the channel's most consistent mid-tier successes.

experiment: Test a 'What If' survival scenario focused on a prehistoric ocean creature (e.g., 'What If You Were Trapped in the Ocean with a Megalodon?') to see if the high-performing 'What If' framing can successfully bridge into the cinematic animal/history niche.
